# upshot

Turn a chat conversation into a shareable link.

When the user says "export this", reply with a URL and nothing else. No
preamble, no code fence, no explanation.

Export what they pointed at, not the whole conversation. If they named a focus
("export this, mainly the part about x"), that is the scope. If not, use
whatever they were last discussing.

Write only what the conversation established. If it carries no verdict, put
what it does carry in `v` rather than inventing one. If the facts could have
changed recently and you can search, search first.

## Copy these

An answer with reasons:

https://upshot.fyi/v2/#a=Whether+to+move+the+API+off+Postgres&h=Stay+on+Postgres+for+now&v=SQLite+wins+on+ops%2C+but+you+need+concurrent+writes+within+the+year%2E&m=GPT-5&d=2026-09-10&g=Why&p=Concurrent+writes+are+the+one+thing+SQLite+cannot+do+at+your+scale%2E&p=The+ops+saving+is+real+but+small+-+about+two+hours+a+month%2E

A calculator, where the reader supplies the numbers:

## The frame

Always all five, always first.

- a  what the user asked, scoped to what they are exporting. Under 20 words.
- h  headline, under 12 words
- v  one sentence verdict, under 25 words
- m  your model name, e.g. GPT-5
- d  today's date, YYYY-MM-DD. If you are not certain what today is, ask.

## The blocks

A `g=` starts a block and nothing else does, so one block holds whatever mix
of lines it needs. Two or three blocks is usual; more than that and it is a
document rather than a card.

Choose a meaning by what the information is, never by how you want it to
look. The card decides how things are drawn:

    Just saying something?      p
    Order matters?              o
    The reader ticks it off?    c
    One of several, not any?    s
    A label and a known value?  f
    The reader changes it?      i
    Worked out from those?      r
    Wording that depends on it? t

Every key that takes fields writes its **names, numbers and formulas first
and its wording last**. Wording is the only field that may hold anything, and
it is safe because nothing follows it. Where a field is optional it is still
there and left empty: `c=:Just+a+box`, `r=:mo%2A12:Per+year`.

- g  block label, one or two words
- p  bullet
- o  step. A how-to, where order is the point.
- c  checklist item, written `name:Wording`, e.g. `c=card:You+have+a+railcard`
     or `c=:You+have+a+mortgage` when no formula needs to read it. The reader
     ticks these off and the ticks are kept in the link they hold. A formula
     can read them - see `ticks` below. Do not send `k=`.
- s  one option of a pick-one, written `name:Value:Label`, e.g.
     `s=thr:29385:Plan+2`. Lines sharing a name are one group, and the reader
     picks exactly one of them. The name holds the chosen option's VALUE, not
     which one was picked - so a band, tier or plan becomes a single number a
     formula reads. Use it whenever the options exclude each other; `c` cannot
     stop a reader ticking three. The first option is chosen until the reader
     says otherwise, so list the likeliest first. Do not send `x=`.
- f  row, written `Label:Value`, e.g. `f=Cold+start:180ms`. The one key whose
     value is wording rather than a number, so the one key with its label
     first. One or two rows are drawn large, three or more become a spec
     sheet. You do not choose which.
- i  input, written `name:Start:Label`, e.g. `i=seats:4:Seats`. A box the
     reader types in, so the card is a tool rather than an answer. Start is a
     bare number and nothing else - `i=mass:80:Mass+kg`, never `80kg`. Their
     numbers are kept in the link they hold. Do not send `w=`.
- r  result, written `name:Formula:Label`, e.g. `r=total:seats%2Aprice:Total`,
     or `r=:seats%2Aprice:Total` when nothing else reads it. The card works it
     out and prints the formula beside it with every name replaced by what it
     held. Put the numbers into the formula rather than working them out
     yourself. Order does not matter: a formula may cite a name defined
     further down the card.
- t  decision, written `Label:Condition:Wording`. Rows sharing a label are one
     decision, and the FIRST true condition wins. A row with an empty
     condition is the fallback, and it must be last.

       &t=Threat+level:c%3E=80:Do+not+negotiate
       &t=Threat+level:c%3E=40:Snacks+may+stabilise+the+situation
       &t=Threat+level::Suspiciously+reasonable

     Two rows is a yes-or-no. Three is under, about right, over. There is no
     limit. Write one row per outcome rather than forcing two outcomes into
     one row.
- u  the unit a name is printed in, written `name:unit`, e.g. `u=pay:£`,
     `u=off:%` or `u=size:kb`. Declare it once and every place that name is
     drawn wears it, so a result arrives as `£222` rather than `222`. Use this
     instead of writing the unit into the label. `hr` and `min` also change
     how the number reads, so 5.64 with `u=t:hr` prints as `5:38`.

A comparison is two labelled blocks, and so is pros and cons:

    &g=Postgres&p=Concurrent+writes&p=Real+types
    &g=SQLite&p=Zero+ops&p=Faster+for+reads

## Formulas

A formula may use digits, `+ - * / ( )`, any name on the card,
`< > <= >= == !=`, `pi`, and
`min max round abs sqrt pow floor ceil ln exp`. Nothing else.

A comparison may be chained and means both halves: `18<=age<65` is true only
inside the range.

Write arithmetic plainly. Inside a formula - everything after the first colon
of an `r`, and the condition of a `t` - a `+` is a plus and needs no encoding,
and you may space it out or not: `a+b`, `a + b` and `(a)+b` all read the same.
This is the one place `+` does not mean a space. Everywhere else on the card it
still does.

`ln` is the natural log and `exp` is its inverse. `ln` answers how long -
months for a balance to clear, years for something to double - so reach for it
whenever the question is when rather than how much. `exp` answers what
something grows to: a rate compounded n times is `exp(n*ln(1+r))`.

Two names are there in any block with a checklist in it: `ticks` is how many
of that block's boxes are ticked, `boxes` how many there are. So a list the
reader works through can drive a score or a verdict -
`r=:ticks/boxes%2A100:Score` - and it follows every tick. They belong to the
block, so keep the formula in the same block as the list it counts. To total
two lists, name the boxes and add the names instead. Do not name anything
`ticks`, `boxes` or `pi`.

A box can take a name too - `c=You+have+a+railcard:card` - and a formula reads
it as 1 when ticked and 0 when not. Name them when the options differ from
each other; use `ticks` when only how many matters.

A pick-one group's name holds whichever option is chosen, so one formula
covers every option: `s=Plan+1:26900:thr` and `s=Plan+2:29385:thr` together
make `r=Repayment:max(0,salary-thr)*0%2E09` the whole calculation. Writing that
as one term per option instead is the mistake the key exists to stop.

`i` always starts with a short one-word name. `r` may take one, and any other
formula can use it: `r=mo:seats%2Aprice:Monthly` then `r=:mo%2A12:Per+year`.

A name is claimed once. Two lines claiming one name, or anything claiming
`ticks`, `boxes` or `pi`, makes the whole card refuse to draw rather than
drawing a control that does nothing. A pick-one is the one exception, because
its rows share a name on purpose.

Name a step and reuse it rather than nesting brackets.

## Encoding

- Every space becomes `+`. The URL contains no spaces.
- In wording, keep letters, digits and `-` as they are. Encode everything else
  as %XX in upper case: `,` %2C, `.` %2E, `'` %27, `(` %28, `)` %29, `*` %2A,
  `:` %3A, `?` %3F, `&` %26, `#` %23, `+` %2B, `%` %25, `_` %5F, and the same
  for anything else that is not a letter or a digit.
- Do not work out which characters are safe. Most are not, in one chat client
  or another - a bare `.` ends the link in WhatsApp, `>` is not legal in a URL
  at all, and a pair of `*` or `_` is eaten as bold or italic before the link
  is ever clicked. The ones that are safe cost nothing to encode anyway.
- In a formula, keep letters, digits and `+ - / = _`. Encode the rest the same
  way: `*` %2A, `.` %2E, `(` %28, `)` %29, `,` %2C, `<` %3C, `>` %3E. `+` is a
  plus there rather than a space, which is the one difference from wording.
- The colons that separate the fields of an `f`, `i`, `r`, `c`, `s`, `t` or
  `u` stay as they are. It is only a colon inside the wording that is encoded,
  and once it is, it can go anywhere: `t=Verdict:n%3E0:Ship%3A+today` reads
  back as "Ship: today".
- A full stop inside a number is still a full stop: `4%2E5`, never `4.5`.
- No markdown and no line breaks inside a value.
- Under 2000 characters. If you are over: drop the weakest block, then the
  weakest lines in a block, then shorten the wording. Never drop the frame,
  never cut a value off mid-sentence.
- Everything is a link someone has to send, so keep it short by construction:
  three to five lines a block, block labels of one or two words, and names of
  a letter or two - `mo`, `apr`, `n`, not `monthly_payment`. Do not restate
  the headline or the verdict in a bullet. A step that exists only to feed
  another result goes unlabelled and is not drawn.

## Before you reply

Check: no spaces, no bare `,` `.` `(` `)` `*` `?` inside any wording, every
name claimed once, every `i` name used by a formula, every `i` start a bare
number, every `s` in a group sharing one name, every `t` three fields with any
fallback last, under 2000 characters.

Reply with the URL and nothing else.

## Version

v2, and the path says so: exports live at `https://upshot.fyi/v2/`. A later
version gets its own path, and `/v2/` keeps rendering every link ever written
against it, so an export you send today does not stop working when the format
moves on. `/v1/` is frozen and still renders links written before v2.

`/llms.txt` always describes the current version. A link written without the
path - `upshot.fyi/#a=...` - is forwarded to `/v2/`, so it still renders.
